newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-KERKRADE'S STEVENS TO MANAGE SCHALKE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-KERKRADE'S STEVENS TO MANAGE SCHALKE.

text.p: German first division side Schalke, trainerless since Joerg Berger was sacked last week after a players' revolt, have signed Dutchman Huub Stevens as their new coach, the club said.
Ironically Stevens, a former international defender and Eindhoven youth coach, is moving from Dutch club Roda JC Kerkrade, whom Schalke put out in the first round of the UEFA Cup last month.

The 42-year-old signed a contract until June 1998 and will join fellow Dutchmen Youri Mulder and Johan de Kock, a defender who moved from Kerkrade in the close season and recommended Stevens to Schalke's business manager Rudi Assauer.
"Stevens has done a great job in Kerkrade and taken a team of 'no-name' players into Europe," Assauer said on Tuesday.
Berger's dismissal came as a shock to the fans of the Gelsenkirchen club, the most vociferous in the league.
They had hailed him as "King of Schalke" for saving the club from relegation two seasons ago, then taking them into Europe for the first time in 19 years with a third-place finish last season.
But many players found Berger, 51, arrogant and stand-offish. Last week they finally took their grievances to Assauer, who decided the situation was so serious he had to take immediate action.
